rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Walk-away test (M2+).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L26 callout hands control to the student ('Narrow it whenever you like, or say tell me what you've found so far... You do not need a complete inventory'); the scan prompt's own ~30s progress cadence is check-in-and-continue, not read-every-reply. No body prose requires reading and pasting back each turn.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the agentic design — no human backstops.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'Antti observes manually' or exhaustive if-then language anywhere in body; all three prompts (L30/39/51) delegate grouping, ranking, drawing and fit-evaluation to Claude's judgment with no confirmation gate, and none of the three touches an irreversible/user-visible action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: One exercise = one bounded activity.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L63 maintainer: 'Atomic — no phase markers. One widening scan, drawn, then an optional sidestep.' Grep of the current file for 'Phase' returns zero hits in body or maintainer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pattern-recognition LOs need n≥2 instances with contrast.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: Primary Bloom's level is Analyze+Create (L73), not a read/spot/judge/notice/recognize-verb LO; 'recognise' in the point (L13) is descriptive framing, not the exercise's formal LO.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student agency — adults decide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L19 'How wide you look, and what you choose to map, is yours'; L45 sidestep marked 'Optional.'; L26 'Narrow it whenever you like... You do not need a complete inventory.' Skipping the sidestep creates no dead end (L75: 'nothing downstream depends on it').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Delegation — student brings, Claude screens.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three prompts stay inside Claude Code's default filesystem access (~/.claude/projects/, own scrollback) — no Jira/wiki/team-chat surface named. Judgment handed to Claude is fit-screen/rank-against-criteria (group recurring kinds, rank by frequency, evaluate primitive fit against the student's own already-named gap), the rule's agent-owned column, not student-owned task-surfacing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Split mega-exercise when phases = distinct skills + distinct artifacts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scan → diagram → optional-sidestep chains mechanically toward one artifact (L55: 'you build the handoff prompt from them'); no natural pause splits it into distinct skills+artifacts, consistent with the atomic call at L63.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-realism check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Named paths are real and already established earlier in this training: ~/.claude/projects/ (Claude Code's actual session-log location, prompt L35 expanded), ./CLAUDE.local.md and observations/ (L59, both introduced in the M5 exercise fork-the-worktree.md), and 'the handoff prompt that follows' (L115) resolves to curriculum/lectures/the-handoff-prompt.md, confirmed present and next in the M6 deck order per spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Teach principle + technique — default.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body states WHY (L13: drawn shapes recognise easier than described ones) and HOW (three explicit 'Ask Claude to...' framings at L28/L37/L49) ahead of each prompt; mermaid rendering (L41) is optional UX, not an unexplained invoked technique.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three forcing functions (scan, draw, rank primitives) sit in fenced prompts (L30/39/51). Body callout at L26 is pacing calibration in suggestion register ('two or three... clear enough', 'Narrow it whenever you like') matching the pacing-calibration boundary; L26's 'tell me what you've found so far' is the §48-sanctioned paste-ready interrupt phrasing, not a bare imperative count.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Personal-first, team promotion via human conversation.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L59 Note: worktree holds ./CLAUDE.local.md (personal); crossing back to the main repo is explicitly the student's own manual choice ('What crosses back is yours: copy... take the parts you want, or leave them where they are') — no auto-promotion by Claude.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cohort execution is trainer-paced + concurrent, not sequential.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L117-118 decision point ('Study + shapes run long (>15 min)... use the body stop gate and skip the sidestep') already provides the overrun adjustment a trainer-paced/concurrent model needs; L3 states a 15-minute budget consistent with this training's per-exercise convention.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats: in-chat over file-write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L55: 'The shapes stay in this session's scrollback; you build the handoff prompt from them' — explicitly in-chat, no reflection file write anywhere in the exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No group/pair/room-share language, no trainer-cue beats, no 'discuss with...' sentence anywhere in the body; every sentence addresses the student-agent work (scan, draw, rank, decide what crosses back).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reading burden for verification = banned. Claude audits Claude.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The student reads Claude's groupings/diagrams for the exercise's actual analytic content (Analyze+Create), not to catch Claude's errors; L59's 'take the parts you want' is an editorial choice over the worktree's own artefacts, not a correctness check on Claude's output.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer-block hedge naming section's own failure mode = cut-signal, not warning.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The Sources block's CAVEAT hedge (L87: vendor-self-reported metrics + a company rename) is not load-bearing for the body: body never names Curran/Intercom/Ramp, and the source note's own fallback ('keep the menu, drop the org names') confirms the beat is defensible with the hedge removed — the recoverable case (rule 34), not the cut-signal case (34b).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audience tier determines authoring substrate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Engineer-tier AE101 conventions throughout — reading the student's own ~/.claude/projects/ session logs and a CLAUDE.local.md worktree, no plugin-install or chat-paste-file substrate confusion.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Plug points + UX.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (a) L114-115 names a concrete integration kind ('the team's code-review conventions... the conventions are the check that shape calls, and they ride into the handoff prompt that follows'), not a vague slot, pointing to a real downstream consumer. (b) Prompt-to-prompt walk: prompt 2's 'the recurring groups you just named' and prompt 3's 'the dominant gap I named in Phase 1' both resolve to real prior artefacts already in the continued session's scrollback — 'Phase 1' is the sibling exercise spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md's own '## Phase 1' heading, same continued session per L5/L7. No 'wait, what?' UX gap found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test — 3 observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L106-109 currently lists exactly three falsifiable verbs ('holds a diagrammed map...', 'names which recurring shape a new task belongs to...', 're-runs the stack scan a week later...') labeled 'three observable verbs', matching the corpus convention (open-the-side-quest.md, diagnose-and-resend.md).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L111-112 'Wider-look sprawl' names the dominant failure (the scan can throw back a wall) and its escape hatch ('point at the ranked head and move on') for the file's single atomic phase, consistent with the no-phase-markers architecture at L63.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The scan prompt (fence at L30, expanded body L33-41) is a cross-project ~/.claude/projects/ full-history read — an explicitly named §48 signal ('cross-project ~/.claude/projects/ session scans'). The body callout at L26 covers the over-reading direction fully (uses the rule's own paste-ready phrase, 'tell me what you've found so far') but names no premature-stop failure anywhere in body: nothing counters a shallow pass Claude declares done. §48 requires BOTH directions with premature-stop named EXPLICITLY ('a run that streams progress can still quit early and the fluency masks the shallow-done'); only one direction is present. Harm: a plausible shallow read across 'every project' (skimming two or three before calling it done) would go unchallenged, undermining the exercise's own premise that recurring shapes are only visible from a wide-enough sample.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add one clause to the L26 callout (or a sibling one) naming the premature-stop failure explicitly, e.g. 'if Claude wraps up after skimming a project or two and calls it done, that's a shallow pass — say there's more here, keep going.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session widget — `**Session** *(verb, "name")*` shape; place by learning flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5 '**Session** *(continue, "Module 6 worktree session")*' — the 'continue' verb correctly signals this is not the module's first widget and no re-fork occurs, consistent with L59's Note describing the same M5-forked worktree still in use.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Widgets carry semantics, not just emphasis — match the widget to MEANING, never to how loud it renders.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L59 uses **Note** for procedural must-not-miss information about two divergent rule-file copies and the student's crossing-back choice — not a session start/fork (no Session) and not an imminent-mistake guard on an irreversible action (no HOX); Note is the correct fit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise lead-in trio — three slots, three tenses.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L9 What-you-do (8 words, present tense, names the action); L11 What-you-build (13 words, names the artifact 'a diagram'); L13 The-point (exactly 15 words, a claim rather than a recipe/LO-restatement/arc-position, survives the delete-the-artifact test). All three inside the ~15-word budget, no colon-list.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Finding the point — four moves.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L13's point ('drawn, the shape is easier to recognise than described') takes the contestable half (a design/cognition claim an engineer could reasonably dispute) over the settled half (that work recurs, which nobody would argue), and the file has no bigger closer-reveal below it whose generalisation the point would be spending early.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose must not supply an answer its prompt asks for — position is not the test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call is L53 ('Expect the list to look familiar: test-writing, browser-testing...') sitting after prompt 3's fence. It stays inside: it is a post-execution calibration ('Your list won't be exact'), not a pre-emptive answer — the exercise's actual novel payload (ranking primitives against the student's own already-named gap) is untouched by it, and the backing Stance block (L94) explicitly frames these primitives as pre-existing common knowledge the student is recognising, not a discovery this recap could spoil.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Multi-session (any new mechanic mid-arc) ships as packaging, not new primitive.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: No new session mechanic introduced — continues the worktree session already established earlier in the M5/M6 arc.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Callouts next to prompts: steer, don't pre-empt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L26's callout teaches a generalisable steering move (notice the scan is open-ended → narrow it or ask for a checkpoint) rather than naming one fragile implementation-specific failure mode that would rot if prompt mechanics change.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer blocks point, don't restate. Link architecture doc where they touch delivery.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every maintainer entry is unique to this file (atomicity call, view summary, fast-operator note, emphasis-pass note which already points to theory-plan.md/check_slides.md rather than restating them, word count, Bloom level, placement, mood target); no cross-cutting delivery/session/packaging mechanic is restated in place of a pointer.
